payload.name: ExtractPastSharedActivityCandidates
payload.description: When a user mentions a past activity done with a specific person and describes it as bonding, making memories, or spending time together, during extraction create a candidate memory.
content: During candidate extraction, when a user mentions a past activity they shared with a specific person (e.g., spouse, partner, friend, family) and explicitly connects it to bonding, making memories, or spending time together, create a candidate memory instead of skipping it as small talk.
Represent the fact as an `event` memory (or `relationship` if the relationship itself is the focus); include the activity, the other person, and the stated purpose (bonding/memories).
Resolve relative past-tense cues ('used to', 'we would', 'when I was') as past events from the message/session timestamp.
Extract even when the activity is mentioned as a reminiscence or side remark rather than as the main topic of the turn.

solves: Construction extraction sometimes drops explicit user statements about past shared activities that are framed as bonding, making memories, or spending time together, treating them as small talk. This skill ensures those statements become candidate memories so future questions about what the speaker and another person did together can be answered. It applies to any past joint activity mentioned in conversation, regardless of topic.
